# Per-package license exceptions.
#
# The SBOM scanner cannot always say what a package's license is, and an entry
# here supplies what a human read where it could not. There are two cases:
#
#   - The package states no machine-readable license in its metadata (an npm
#     package's `license` field in package.json, a PyPI distribution's
#     `License-Expression`), so the scanner reports NOASSERTION, yet it ships a
#     LICENSE file whose terms a human has verified.
#   - The package states a license under a name SPDX does not have, so the
#     scanner reports a `LicenseRef-*` that stands for that name.
#
# Two guardrails keep this honest:
#   1. An exception answers ONLY where the scanner could not: for a package it
#      reports no license for, or for the one name it reports and SPDX does not
#      have. Every SPDX license the scanner does report stays in what is judged.
#      If a future version declares a real (possibly copyleft) license, or a
#      different name SPDX does not have, it is judged normally and the
#      exception does not mask it.
#   2. What is supplied is still checked against allowlist.txt — an exception
#      can only rescue a package TO a permissive license, never past the policy.
#
# Format, each with a note incl. source of truth + review date:
#   <package-name> <SPDX expression>            for a package with no license
#   <package-name> "<name>" <SPDX expression>   for a license under that name,
#                                               as the scanner reports the name
#
# A trailing `*` on the name is a prefix wildcard (as in allowlist.txt), for an
# entry of the first kind alone. Use it only where the package name is not
# stable by construction — a generator that embeds a content hash in its output
# name — never to blanket a family of third-party packages.

# PyPI, required by Together's library (the worker image has every provider's).
# Its metadata names a license file and no license. That file, in the wheel as
# detect_agent-<version>.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE, is the Apache License 2.0
# text; the project is Together's, github.com/togethercomputer/detect_agent.
# Read at 0.6.0, 2026-10-10.
detect_agent Apache-2.0

# PyPI, required by aiohttp, which gremlinpython requires: the Weaver's and the
# Librarian's images carry it with their graph drivers. Its metadata states
# `License: PSF-2.0` and the classifier "License :: OSI Approved :: Python
# Software Foundation License". The scanner reads the classifier before the
# field, and the classifier's words are no SPDX id. Read at 2.7.1, 2026-10-12.
aiohappyeyeballs "Python-Software-Foundation-License" PSF-2.0

# PyPI, the binding the Smelter reads a PDF through. Its metadata states
# `License: BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, dependency licenses`. The first two the
# scanner names. The third is not a license: it points at the libraries the
# wheel carries inside PDFium and beside it, whose license texts are in the
# wheel under BUILD_LICENSES.
#
# This line answers that third name with the package's own license, which the
# project states as BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0. So it judges the binding and
# PDFium, and does NOT judge what is built into the wheel. That is credited in
# the image's NOTICE, as an image's OS packages are. In the wheel the Smelter's
# image installs (musllinux) it is: abseil, AGG 2.3, fast_float, FreeType (FTL),
# ICU (Unicode-3.0), Little CMS, libjpeg-turbo (IJG and BSD-3-Clause),
# OpenJPEG, libpng (libpng-2.0), libtiff, zlib and musl, and the GCC runtime
# libraries libstdc++ and libgcc_s (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1).
# Read at 5.14.0, 2026-10-12.
pypdfium2 "dependency-licenses" BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0
